notes: Both agree that coexpression of NDC80, HSK3, and CLB3 enhances sister chromatid segregation. High overlap (C90, C91, C92, C93) with consistent SUPPORTED status.

Both rate claims about outer kinetochore regulation in other organisms (C119-C123) as UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewers note prior S. pombe work and question novelty claims; LLM notes speculative connections require validation.
Both agree on centromeric cohesin protection findings (C55-C64). Peer reviewers describe this as 'important and new discovery' with 'impeccable' data; LLM finds strong mechanistic evidence.
Both support monopolin localization defect findings (C50-C54). Peer reviewers acknowledge as 'novel observations'; LLM finds strong evidence from chromosome spreads and Western blots.
Both support outer kinetochore downregulation findings (C84-C88). Peer reviewers describe data as 'impeccable'; LLM finds strong evidence from ribosome profiling and correlation with phenotypes.

LLM supports central findings (C3, C4, C95, C127) as well-supported by extensive data. Peer reviewers question physiological relevance of overexpression approach and state 'some conclusions remain speculative.'

Both support cyclin-specific effects on spindle formation and attachments (C34-C41, C45). Peer reviewers acknowledge 'cleverly designed experiments' showing bipolar spindle development; LLM finds strong evidence from live-cell imaging.
Both support sister chromatid segregation findings (C46-C48). Peer reviewers acknowledge premature attachments disrupt normal segregation; LLM finds strong evidence from timing analysis.

LLM supports timing vs. protein level conclusions (C31-C33). Peer reviewers express concern about lack of comprehensive Western blot data and question whether differences reflect specificity or levels.

LLM supports cyclin-specific CDK effects (C42-C44). Peer reviewers question whether phenotypic differences are due to 'kinase protein levels or activities' and whether Clb4's limited effects reflect 'specificity or levels.'

Both support restoration of monopolin function by disrupting microtubule-kinetochore interactions (C72-C74). Peer reviewers implicitly accept as part of novel findings; LLM finds strong evidence from ndc80-1 experiments.
LLM supports two independent mechanisms (C114-C115). Peer reviewers state 'it is an overstatement' and suggest alternative interpretations involving transcriptional/translational regulation by CDK.

LLM supports requirement for both Clb3-CDK and outer kinetochore components (C116, C118). Peer reviewers note 'important paradox' that artificial kinetochore assembly doesn't affect segregation without CLB3 and state physiological role 'remains completely unproven.'

LLM supports claim that recombination is unaffected (C49). Peer reviewers directly challenge this, stating 'FigureS1E shows that recombination is not normal' with earlier timing and lower levels, calling it 'a contradiction that needs to be addressed.'

Both support restoration of cohesin protection by disrupting microtubule-kinetochore interactions (C76-C78). Peer reviewers acknowledge disruption of pericentric cohesion as key finding; LLM finds strong evidence from ndc80-1 and dam1-1 experiments.

LLM supports timing conclusions (C30). Peer reviewers raise concerns that 'CUP-CLB3 is induced so early that cells may still be in S phase' and request FACS analysis, expressing uncertainty about developmental timing.
LLM supports outer kinetochore downregulation timing (C82-C83). Peer reviewers question timing, noting induction may occur during S phase and requesting FACS data to validate developmental stage.

LLM supports mechanistic interpretation about premature microtubule-kinetochore interactions (C70). Peer reviewers question 'physiological relevance' of overexpression experiments for understanding wild-type meiosis.
LLM supports restoration of proper segregation (C80). Peer reviewers question how relevant 'very early, very high expression of Clb3' is for understanding wild-type meiosis.
LLM supports outer kinetochore limiting mechanism (C94). Peer reviewers note 'important paradox' and state physiological role 'remains completely unproven,' suggesting alternative explanations.

LLM supports central finding about preventing premature interactions (C5). Peer reviewers question whether physiological role of outer kinetochore disassembly is proven and note paradox with artificial assembly experiments.

LLM supports correlation between Ndc80 levels and phenotype (C89). Peer reviewers question whether physiological role is to prevent premature connections, noting paradox that artificial assembly alone doesn't affect segregation.
LLM supports outer kinetochore assembly contribution (C115). Peer reviewers state physiological role 'remains completely unproven' and note the paradox requiring both CLB3 and kinetochore components.
Background claims (C1, C2, C6-C27) only evaluated by LLM. These establish foundational knowledge about meiosis mechanisms and are not specifically addressed by peer reviewers.
Sgo1-PP2A localization findings (C65-C67) only evaluated by LLM. Peer reviewers do not specifically address shugoshin localization data.
Mitotic monopolin induction experiment (C71) only evaluated by LLM. Peer reviewers do not specifically comment on this supporting experiment.

Speculative mechanism claims (C98-C99, C102-C105) only evaluated by LLM as UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewers do not specifically address these mechanistic speculations.
Timing-dependent cohesin protection claims (C100-C101) only evaluated by LLM. Peer reviewers do not specifically address the mam1Δ comparison.
Tension-dependent cohesin protection mechanisms (C106-C108) only evaluated by LLM. Peer reviewers do not specifically address these mechanistic discussions.
Broader significance claims (C126, C128) only evaluated by LLM. Peer reviewers do not specifically address the human aneuploidy context or evolutionary conservation statements.
